newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters calls, then cancels news conference.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters calls, then cancels news conference.

text.p: New Zealand First leader Winston Peters called a news conference after Thursday's meeting with the main opposition Labour party, but cancelled it after television cameras started rolling early.

Peters walked out on the journalists gathered in parliament's Bowen House foyer saying an agreement on the conference had been broken when TV3 began filming him looking at an article in the afternoon newspaper about his late night visits to bars and restaurants.
Journalists had earlier been told they were banned from the floor containing New Zealand First's offices and from the floor where the coalition talks are being held.
After Thursday's 80-minute meeting, Labour leader Helen Clark said further formal meetings would be held with New Zealand First next Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.
"We will be getting a lot of work done next week. We are making good progress," Clark said.
"I think realistically there's a lot of detailed policy discussion to go on for another three weeks at least."
She said Labour finance spokesman Michael Cullen did not attend the meeting because he was in Dunedin.
She would not reveal which policy areas had been discussed, but said Labour and New Zealand First had not had any talks on economic policy outside the formal meetings.

New Zealand has a caretaker National Party government after an inconclusive general election on October 12. Nationalist New Zealand First, which holds the balance of power, is negotiating with both National and Labour over the make-up of a new government.

Expanding on her earlier comments about who should attend the APEC meeting in Manila in late November, Clark said it was esesential there was consultation between the caretaker government and the other parties.
Asked if she would support Prime Minister Jim Bolger going if a new govenment was not formed by then, Clark said: "I am strongly opposed to him taking a unilateral decision to go."
